title: Derived global cohomology of finite-field constructible complexes is insensitive to the two algebraic-closure coefficient topologies
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology. On profinite sets with finite jointly surjective covers put $C(P)=\{f\in C(P,\Omega): f(P)\subset F\text{ for some finite }\mathbf Q_\ell\subset F\subset\Omega\}$ and $B(P)=C(P,\Omega)$ [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Write $c:C\to B$ for inclusion, $C_X=p_X^*C$, $B_X=p_X^*B$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Fix a finite intermediate field $E\subset\Omega$, with the restricted norm topology, and put $A=p_X^*\underline E$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. All module categories are internal module categories, with their ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] and derived relative tensor and internal Hom [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Bounded constructible below means the finite constant local model convention [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

For every bounded constructible $V\in D(A)$ let
$$m_V:\operatorname{Res}_{A\to C_X}(C_X\otimes_A^L V)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B_X}(B_X\otimes_A^L V)$$
be the actual morphism in $D(A)$ induced by $c_X$, represented on a flat-term K-flat resolution $P$ by $z\otimes v\mapsto c_X(z)\otimes v$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. On forgetting coefficient actions and applying derived global sections on the small pro-etale site [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology], the morphism
$$R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},m_V):R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},C_X\otimes_A^L V)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B_X\otimes_A^L V)$$
is an isomorphism in the ordinary derived category of abelian groups. This asserts neither that $m_V$ is a sheaf-level isomorphism nor that derived internal Hom commutes with $A\to B_X$. No flatness of $c_X$, completeness of $\Omega$, or finite global cohomological dimension of $k$ is assumed.
